subparts.final_answer: $Scatter plot of Camera B vs Camera A$

mark_breakdown.desc: Correctly plotted points on the Cartesian plane with axes labelled

subparts.solution: Plot the points $(x, y)$ representing (Camera A, Camera B): $(8.5, 7)$, $(8, 6)$, $(9, 7.5)$, $(7, 9)$, $(8.5, 7.5)$, and $(7.5, 6)$ on a scatter plot.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: A scatter plot graphically represents bivariate data by plotting ordered pairs $(x, y)$ on a coordinate plane.
step_by_step: Label the horizontal axis as Camera A and the vertical axis as Camera B.
Choose appropriate scale markings from 5 to 11 on the horizontal axis and 5 to 10 on the vertical axis.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Swapping the $x$ and $y$ variables or incorrectly scaling the axes.

mark_breakdown.desc: Identification of the outlier point and its interpretation

subparts.solution: The point $(7, 9)$ appears to be an outlier. This corresponds to the review scoring camera A a 7, and camera B a 9.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: An outlier in bivariate data is a point that does not follow the general trend or pattern seen in the rest of the data.
step_by_step: Observe the overall pattern of the plotted points.
Identify the point that lies noticeably far from the general cluster, which is $(7, 9)$.
Interpret the coordinates in context: Camera A score of 7 and Camera B score of 9.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Identifying the highest or lowest single value instead of the point deviating from the bivariate trend.
